title: Mitigate tenant egress hairpinning and resolve DNS TTL staleness on Dedicated
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Summary:
Customer escalations surfaced multiple Dedicated tenants intermittently seeing 5xx/connection failures after VPC peering changes or autoscaler-driven capacity moves. Root cause analysis indicates two correlated issues: (1) egress hairpinning when tenant traffic traverses peering hops and is NAT-reflected back into the same tenant VPC, creating sticky conntrack state that invalidates new routes, and (2) our DNS forwarder (CoreDNS layer) holding stale A records beyond expected propagation during peering failovers due to TTL caching combined with conditional forwarders to peer zones. Together these lead to prolonged reachability issues for model endpoints (customers observed 3–15 minute outages depending on TTL).

Observed impact and signals:
- Multiple customer support tickets from enterprise tenants (notably "FinSight") reporting intermittent failures immediately after peering maintenance or autoscaler migrations.
- Grafana: increased 5xx spike on per-tenant ingress/gateway and downstream TCP reset spikes from inference nodes around peering update windows.
- Packet captures show mirrored source/destination pairs with conntrack entries preventing new flows after DNAT reflection.
- CoreDNS metrics show cache hit ratios with A records kept until TTL expiry; conditional forwarders to peered zones were not purging on peering failover.

Repro steps (internal):
1) Create two dedicated tenant VPCs configured with VPC peering and routed egress through a shared NAT gateway.
2) Deploy a simple echo TCP service in tenant A and a client in tenant A that reaches the service via the peered path (hairpin).
3) Trigger route update (simulate peering failover or autoscaler migration) and observe conntrack entries and DNS resolution from the node's resolver.
4) Observe 5xx/errors for new connections until conntrack purge or DNS TTL expiry.

Hypothesis and root cause summary:
- Hairpin flows create DNAT/SNAT state where the kernel conntrack table binds original 5-tuple to a backend IP that becomes invalid after route/peering changes, blocking new connections until state times out.
- CoreDNS conditional forwarder cache was not being invalidated on peering agent's detected failover, relying solely on TTL which ranged 60–900s depending on zone.
- Both issues combined to lengthen outage windows for affected tenants.

Immediate mitigation implemented (hotfix):
- Deployed conntrack cleanup hook in peering controller that proactively runs targeted conntrack flush for affected 5-tuples on detected route change. Hotfix rolled as kube DaemonSet with a conservative rate limit; PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7892.
- Added a short-lived aggressive TTL override for conditional forwarders during failover windows (component-level TTL override), plus explicit cache purge in CoreDNS on peering-controller event. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/networking-config/pull/7901.

Planned permanent fixes and trade-offs:
- Change egress SNAT behavior for dedicated tenants to ensure egress reflection does not produce DNAT loops. This requires a kernel/iproute rule change and adjustments to our NAT gateway logic; trade-off: potential small increase in NAT gateway resource usage due to per-tenant SNAT entries.
- Implement a connection-tracking library integration in the peering agent to maintain and reconcile conntrack state proactively across nodes during migrations (more complex, longer ramp).
- Modify CoreDNS configuration to lower TTL for peered-zone entries by default and add a peering health-hook to trigger immediate cache invalidation. Trade-off: more DNS churn and slightly higher query volume during healthy periods.

Testing and rollout plan:
- Canary 01: Roll conntrack cleanup and CoreDNS cache purge to 3 small tenants (non-production) and monitor 48h. Metrics: per-tenant 5xx, conntrack table churn, DNS query spikes.
- Canary 02: If stable, roll to 15% of tenants during a low-traffic window with increased monitoring and a temporary 30m rollback window.
- Full rollout expected by 2026-03-18 if canaries show <1% increase in transient errors and 80% reduction in prolonged outage windows.

Rollback plan:
- Revert peering-controller DaemonSet and CoreDNS config via Helm rollback. Reintroduce previous behavior and fall back to manual conntrack clears as emergency measure. Support team has a runbook for manual purge for high-priority customers.

Observability & monitoring additions:
- Add Grafana alert: persistent per-tenant 5xx > 2% for 5m after peering event; page SRE on call.
- Add per-tenant DNS cache TTL metric in CoreDNS exporter and a peering-failover event stream in the tracing pipeline.

Postmortem owner and follow-ups:
- Primary owner: Marco Delgado (Networking). Secondary: Priya Natarajan (SRE).
- Follow-ups: ENG-50413 (SNAT redesign), ENG-50414 (conntrack library integration), PM follow-up to update runbooks and customer communication templates.

Artifacts and links:
- Confluence runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/NET/ENG-50412+Egress+Hairpin+Postmortem
- Hotfix PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7892, https://github.com/redwood-inference/networking-config/pull/7901
- Grafana dashboard (tenant-perf): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/tenant-perf/peering-events
- Support tickets: SPT-2026-0312-FINSIGHT, SPT-2026-0313-ACME
steps_to_reproduce: Provision two Dedicated tenant VPCs with VPC peering and shared NAT egress
Deploy echo server in tenant B and a client in tenant A that routes to B via peering
Trigger peering route change (simulate failover or kube pod move) and watch conntrack entries
Attempt new connections from client and observe failures until conntrack purge or DNS TTL expiry
resolution: Hotfix deployed: conntrack cleanup hook + CoreDNS cache purge on peering events. Initial canary shows reduced outage windows from median 7min to <30s for tested tenants. Permanent SNAT redesign and conntrack library integration scoped as follow-up tickets.
